original_interpretation: TI received US$335m CHIPS incentive proceeds in 2025 incl. US$75m direct funding
evidence_found: "In 2025, we received proceeds of $335 million from CHIPS Act incentives, including $75 million in direct funding." correction: Accurate. For context: TI's total 2025 CHIPS cash benefit was US$670m (US$335m cash proceeds plus US$335m of ITC used to reduce income taxes payable); do not read US$335m as the total benefit.

original_interpretation: 26 USC 48D credit is 35% for property placed in service after 31 Dec 2025, raised from 25% by Pub. L. 119-21
evidence_found: 48D(a): "the advanced manufacturing investment credit for any taxable year is an amount equal to 35 percent of the qualified investment"; Amendments: "2025-Subsec. (a). Pub. L. 119-21 substituted "35 percent" for "25 percent"."; Effective date note: "shall apply to property placed in service after December 31, 2025."

original_interpretation: 48D advanced manufacturing facility = primary purpose manufacturing semiconductors or SME
evidence_found: 48D(b)(3): "the term "advanced manufacturing facility" means a facility for which the primary purpose is the manufacturing of semiconductors or semiconductor manufacturing equipment."

original_interpretation: 48D credit does not apply to property whose construction begins after 31 Dec 2026
evidence_found: 48D(e) Termination of credit: "The credit allowed under this section shall not apply to property the construction of which begins after December 31, 2026."

original_interpretation: 48D credit can be elected as a payment against tax (direct pay)

notes: 'Cash payment' is a fair reading: a deemed payment in excess of tax liability is refundable. Election is irrevocable and due with the return (48D(d)).

original_interpretation: CRS: constructing and equipping a leading-edge 5nm logic fab cost ~US$5bn in 2020

TSMC 59.9% and NVIDIA 71.1% already verified.

original_interpretation: Interpretation: manufacturers carry physical capital (capex/revenue TSMC 33%, Micron 42%, TI 26%, ASML 5%); fabless/IP carry supply commitments and R&D
evidence_found: Inputs re-checked: Micron "Expenditures for property, plant, and equipment (15,857)" vs revenue 37,378 = 42.4%; TI capex $4.55bn / revenue $17,682m = 25.7%; ASML PP&E purchases "2025: €1,573.6 million" / €32.7bn net sales = 4.8%; Synopsys R&D 2,479,338 / revenue 7,054,178 = 35.1%; TSMC 33% and NVIDIA US$95.2bn commitments already verified.
correction: The capex ratios are right. The contrast with fabless and IP firms is not shown: no capex/revenue ratio is given for NVIDIA or Synopsys, ASML is an equipment maker not a fabless firm, and high R&D is not unique to fabless/IP (TI R&D is about 12% of revenue). Restate as: sampled fab owners spend 26-42% of revenue on capex vs about 5% at ASML; NVIDIA carries large supply commitments and Synopsys spends about 35% of revenue on R&D.
notes: TSMC/NVIDIA inputs were not re-opened in this run; relied on their existing verified fact-checks.

original_interpretation: Interpretation: demand risk is pushed upstream differently by segment (foundry prepayments/LTAs, fabless deposits/non-cancellable orders, OSAT customers bear materials, distributors protected)
evidence_found: Inputs re-checked: GF "We have entered into multiple LTAs that provide for significant customer commitments in return for capacity reservation commitments from us" (2025 20-F); Amkor "customers are generally responsible for any unused materials we purchase based on such commitments" (2025 10-K); Avnet agreements "typically provide certain protections for product obsolescence and price erosion" (FY2025 10-K). TSMC/NVIDIA inputs already verified.
correction: Each segment fact is supported, but 'pushed upstream' is wrong for most cases: at foundries and OSATs the buyer of capacity (downstream) bears the risk through prepayments, commitments or unused-materials liability, and NVIDIA (the buyer) pays deposits. Only for distributors is the risk pushed upstream to the chip suppliers. Restate as: the evidence shows demand risk is allocated differently by segment.
notes: Amkor 'no binding forecasts' wording confirmed in Amkor filings incl. the 2025 10-K by EDGAR full-text search; GF 20-F also notes GF owes penalties if it cannot meet reserved capacity, so risk is two-way. TSMC/NVIDIA inputs were not re-opened in this run; relied on their existing verified fact-checks.
